newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Austria warns against leaving Slovakia isolated.
newsitem.headline: Austria warns against leaving Slovakia isolated.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima urged the European Union on Wednesday to make sure his country's neighbour Slovakia was not left feeling isolated as the bloc expands to eastern Europe.

"I think it's very important that clear political signals of openness are given towards Slovakia that we do not want it to be isolated," Klima told a news conference after meeting European Commission President Jacques Santer.
Slovakia was one of five applicant eastern bloc countries which the European Commission said last week were not ready to open entry talks with the EU early next year.

Klima said that after initially lobbying for talks with all 10 countries to start at once, Vienna could now accept the Commission's game plan to open just with Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovenia and Estonia.
Vienna had been won round by the Commission's plan to keep those left out involved and let them join talks when they were up to scratch, he said.
Latvia, Lithuania, Bulgaria and Romania were also deemed unready by the EU executive for early entry talks, but Slovakia was the only central European country left out on a limb.
The Commission said that although Slovakia was economically on track, it was the only applicant to have been ruled out for not meeting the EU's political criteria.
The Commission said its main concern was the lack of stability of Slovakia's political institutions, which should guarantee democracy and respect for human rights and minorities.
